messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

message.content: The largest planet that astronomers have confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**. It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius roughly 2½–3 times that of Jupiter—about 20–25 million kilometers across. Its mass is estimated at about 15–20 Jupiter masses, putting it right on the boundary between giant planets and brown dwarfs. No larger “planet‑sized” object has been found yet, though future surveys may discover even bigger ones.
